message:
Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer and Manager, the daily balance now closes in electrical units on your single thermal chain because I recomputed to adopt the curtain door model.

In plain words sun electricity must cover cold plus fans plus controls after dividing cooling heat by hot efficiency. Reusing the single thermal total conduction respiration door pulldown fans (E109) at 13.5 kilowatt-hour thermal per day as conduction 4.87 plus respiration 1.20 plus door 0.169 from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) plus staged pull-down 6.25 for 1000 kilogram from the total produce mass estimate (E49) as 50 crates from the crates for 1 tonne check (E77) staged 12.5 crates per day from the daily crates for 250kg staged intake (E78), divided by Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling per electric power) 1.40 at hot ambient plus fans 0.96 plus controls 0.48 equals 10.4 kilowatt-hour electrical per day in the term-by-term check (E128), which confirms the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111) and supersedes my 10.6 kilowatt-hour per day in the reconciled electrical sum (E91) that used the old 0.44 kilowatt-hour door term, about one household day so everyday scale holds.

Manager, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist and Enclosure and Structural Designer, yield covers that load and night plus cloud is carried by stored charge with shed because I reuse prior sizing. In plain words panels make extra by day and batteries run the night alone. Yield is 3.60 kilowatt peak times 5.00 Peak Sun Hours (PSH, equivalent full-sun hours) times 0.75 derate for heat plus soiling plus wiring equals 13.5 kilowatt-hour per day in the grown-array yield calc (E83), leaving margin 3.10 kilowatt-hour per day over 10.4, about one quarter household use, with equator-facing tilt equal latitude plus 10 degrees and zero shading 9am to 3pm, and night 18 to 6 hours load 3.02 kilowatt-hour with one cloudy day at 30 percent sun still ending at 3.73 kilowatt-hour in the battery autonomy simulation (E95) on 10.0 kilowatt-hour usable Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4, rechargeable battery chemistry), needing 3.77 kilowatt-hour nominal at 80 percent Depth of Discharge (DoD, usable fraction) for night alone in the nominal sizing calc (E96), with compressor surge about 1.80 kilowatt against 2 kilowatt inverter and charge current 75.0 ampere at 48 volt in the charge current calc (E97) with Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT, solar charge optimizer) plus Low-Voltage Disconnect (LVD, automatic battery protector that sheds load) shed of new intake per your refusal rule.

Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer and Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, solar-only means fixed split array plus electrochemical storage mandatory plus washable maintenance. In plain words only sun powers the store, ice cannot start the motor at night, and dust must be washed off. Photovoltaic (PV, solar electricity) stays 2 modules on roof gantry plus 7 on separate ground frame for 17.6 square metres in the nine-module footprint for grown array (E84) from module size in the PRBS 400W Monocrystalline Photovoltaic Panels source, direct-drive ice from my pumping analogy stays only as peak cold buffer because it cannot run fans plus controls plus compressor start, and maintenance is panel washing plus vented battery box plus MPPT checks. From my discipline the BD50F Direct Current Compressor R134a, 12-24V DC source (E102) that Cold-Chain Refrigeration Engineer put on the board confirms my conversion basis, because its 60 degree condensing hot rating justifies using derated COP 1.40 instead of catalogue COP for sizing wire power and surge.

My position is ready on version two, because term-by-term electrical load with stated hot COP, derated yield, and night plus cloudy autonomy with surge and shed now close on shared ids except field pull test and 43 degree pull-down bench test needing built hardware.
